Apple today announced that it will no longer migrate iCloud+ "Hide My Email" addresses to a new domain, reversing a change it announced just two months ago. Here's the detail.

Apple Withdraws Controversial iCloud+ "Hide My Email" Domain Change

In mid-June this year, Apple announced that "Sign in with Apple" and "Hide My Email" would adopt a new shared email domain, with addresses for both services migrating to private.icloud.com.

Currently, "Sign in with Apple" uses privaterelay.appleid.com, while "Hide My Email" addresses use the icloud.com domain, the same as regular iCloud email accounts.

This makes it harder for websites to identify and block "Hide My Email" aliases, since blocking at the domain level could also block regular iCloud email addresses.

Precisely for this reason, when Apple decided to migrate "Hide My Email" to the new private.icloud.com domain, it immediately sparked controversy, as the move would make it easier for platforms to block this privacy feature, significantly affecting users who do not wish to provide their real email addresses when creating accounts or filling out forms.

Apple today announced it is shelving the planned "Hide My Email" domain change. In a developer update, the company stated: "After further consideration and review of community feedback, iCloud+ 'Hide My Email' addresses will continue to use icloud.com as before."

The company also stated that from later this year, "new 'Sign in with Apple' addresses will be issued from private.icloud.com instead of the existing privaterelay.appleid.com," and noted that "existing addresses on privaterelay.appleid.com will continue to function normally, forwarding mail to users without interruption."

Apple advises developers using "Sign in with Apple" to ensure their account systems, email verification logic, and whitelists accept both the private.icloud.com and the existing privaterelay.appleid.com domains.
